attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as NAT egress router for node2/node3 on a private 10.50.50.0/24 network reachable via their second NIC (eth1 on node1, ens7 on node2/node3). Added VyOS source NAT masquerade rule 100 (source 10.50.50.0/24 -> outbound eth0) and committed/saved config. On node2/node3, statically configured ens7 (10.50.50.11/.12) and added a low-metric (50) default route via node1 (10.50.50.254) on ens7, so ordinary process traffic egresses through node1's NAT while their pre-existing management-network route remains as a fallback. Verified NAT translation via conntrack on node1 (src 10.50.50.11/.12 translated to node1's WAN IP 10.100.62.10) and confirmed internet reachability (ping/curl) from both node2 and node3 sourced on ens7. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id baselines on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time) via native `reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed after reconnecting, and verified post-restart that NAT config persisted on node1 (VyOS `show nat` still shows rule 100) and that node2/node3 retained their static IP/route config and successfully reached the internet through node1 again.
